rules.title: San Francisco ban on qualifying algorithmic rent devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Tenants can sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties, and each month of use for each affected unit may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each unit-month may be a separate violation

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords using qualifying algorithmic devices; no building coverage limits stated.

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits qualifying algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation, with unit/month exposure
rules.review_note: Secondary source; verify against the code text.
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert (Morgan Lewis, Aug. 21, 2026). The ordinance is at issue in Gomez v. Greystar Management Services LLC (N.D. Cal.).

rules.title: San Diego ban on algorithmic rent-setting (§§ 98.1101–98.1104)
rules.requirement: Prohibits use of RealPage-type algorithmic rent tools. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and penalties, and each month and affected rental property may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation; each month and affected property potentially a separate violation
rules.quoted_span: Similar prohibition and private remedy of up to $1,000 per violation
rules.review_note: Secondary source; the prohibition's details are described only briefly.
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. The ordinance is at issue in Keller v. UDR Inc. (S.D. Cal.).

rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms. Violations recur by unit and month, and private remedies are available.
rules.effective_date_note: This alert states 'effective January 2026' (month only). The organizer brief says the ordinance text gives March 1, 2026.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies
rules.conflict_note: Open question on the effective date: this alert says January 2026, while the organizer brief says the ordinance text gives March 1, 2026. This document does not resolve it.
rules.review_note: Check the ordinance text for the effective date. No penalty amount is stated.
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. RealPage, Inc. v. City of Berkeley et al. (N.D. Cal.) was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice Jan. 14, 2026.

rules.title: Santa Ana ordinance on automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing. Tenants may bring private claims, and violations are counted per month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.review_note: The Santa Ana Municipal Code section is not given.

rules.title: Philadelphia ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Prohibits use of RealPage-type services. An aggrieved person may elect statutory damages or treble actual damages, plus equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs.
rules.key_value: $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, plus fees and costs
rules.quoted_span: Private remedies include treble actual damages or $2,000 per violation
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. The ordinance is at issue in Liu v. Willow Bridge Property Co. and Jahanbakhsh v. Greystar.

rules.title: Minneapolis ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data
rules.requirement: Prohibits algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates. Tenants may pursue civil actions.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data to advise on vacancy or rental rates; tenants may pursue civil actions.

rules.title: Providence ban on rent-setting algorithms
rules.requirement: Prohibits use of rent-setting algorithms and algorithmic rent-setting devices. The city solicitor may bring enforcement actions, with civil penalties, costs and attorney fees.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $500 per day per violation, plus costs and attorney fees
citation_aliases: Providence Code of Ordinances ch. 13, art. X, §§ 13-69–13-73
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits the use of rent-setting algorithms; the city expressly linked the measure to software such as RealPage
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. The ordinance is at issue in City of Providence v. Audubon Capital Partners, LLC (Providence Mun. Ct.).

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Prohibits a landlord's use of algorithmic rent coordination services, with public and private enforcement.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.review_note: The organizer brief notes that New Jersey's FAIR Act may preempt this ordinance. This document does not discuss that.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on software-based rent coordination
rules.requirement: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
citation_aliases: Hoboken City Code ch. 158, Art. II
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.review_note: The organizer brief notes that New Jersey's FAIR Act may preempt this ordinance. This document does not discuss that.

rules.title: Seattle ban on algorithmic coordinating services
rules.requirement: Prohibits specified algorithmic coordinating services in connection with multifamily rental housing.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits specified coordinating services; penalties may reach $7,500 per violation
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. The ordinance is at issue in Nicolas v. Essex Management Corp. and Romano v. UDR Inc. (W.D. Wash.).

rules.title: King County algorithmic rent-setting remedies
rules.requirement: Injured renters may seek actual damages, statutory damages and attorney fees under the county's algorithmic rent-pricing chapter.
rules.key_value: Up to $7,500 per violation plus actual damages and attorney fees
rules.quoted_span: Injured renters may seek actual damages, up to $7,500 per violation and attorney fees.
rules.review_note: The source describes only the remedy, not the prohibited conduct.

rules.title: Spokane ban on purchasing algorithmic coordinating services
rules.requirement: Prohibits landlords from purchasing algorithmic coordinating services. The city enforces through civil penalties.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from purchasing algorithmic coordinating services; city enforcement includes civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation.

rules.title: Portland ban on algorithm-assisted rental price coordination
rules.requirement: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination. For owners of 16 or more units, private remedies are available.
rules.key_value: Greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation (private remedy, owners of 16+ units)

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Private remedies apply to owners of 16 or more units
coverage.summary: Private remedies apply to owners of 16 or more units; the source does not say whether the prohibition has a size threshold.
coverage.owner_conditions: Owners of 16 or more units (private remedies)

rules.quoted_span: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination; for owners of 16 or more units, private remedies include the greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation.

rules.title: Rockville ban on algorithmic devices and shared competitor information
rules.requirement: Prohibits landlords from using algorithmic devices and shared competitor information to set rent, fees, or other rental terms.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using algorithmic devices and shared competitor information to set rent, fees, or other rental terms.

no_rule_findings.finding: The source says algorithmic rent-pricing regulations remain pending in Montgomery County, Maryland, Evanston, Illinois, and Rhode Island, with no bill numbers or terms given.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: Many other municipal regulations remain pending, including in Montgomery County, Maryland; Evanston, Illinois; and Rhode Island.

result.doc_summary: A secondary law-firm alert (Morgan Lewis, Aug. 21, 2026) on follow-on litigation under state and local bans on algorithmic rent-setting. A table lists ordinances in San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley, Santa Ana, Philadelphia, Minneapolis, Providence, Jersey City, Hoboken, Seattle, King County, Spokane, Portland and Rockville, with effective dates (mostly month only) and penalties or remedies. Rockville's takes effect Jan. 1, 2027. Montgomery County, Evanston and Rhode Island measures are pending. The Berkeley effective date (January 2026 in this alert) is an open question per the organizer brief.
